chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hammad ibn Isa, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at a mattress in the house of a man and said: 'There is a mattress for the man, and a mattress for his family, and a mattress for his guest, and a mattress for the Satan.'
ai.seo_question: What are the four purposes of a mattress according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) categorizes the single mattress into four spiritual states: for the owner, his family, his guest, and the Satan. This narration underscores the concept of *khushu'* (devotion) in domestic life, where a bed used merely for physical gratification or neglect of duties becomes a domain for Satan, whereas its use for rest, family bonding, and hospitality elevates it to an act of worship. This reflects the Shia emphasis on transforming mundane household activities into spiritual opportunities through mindful intention.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin dawood Al Minqary, from Hammad Bin Isa who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> looked at a mattress in a house of a man, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is a mattress for the man, and a mattress for his family, and a mattress for his guest, and a mattress for the Satan<sup>la</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasaniy from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqariy from Hammad ibn ‘Isa who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once looked at the furnishings in the house of a man, and said, ‘A spreading for the man, one for his wife, one for his guests and one for Satan.’”
